no_code_body: The project has no gear repository and no GitHub source whose Cargo manifests could be read.
nothing_missing_body: Every capability the documents ask for is filled by a gear in {repo}.
against_code_hint: The documents against the crates {repo} depends on and the gears it declares.
decide_in_product: A decision about which gear fills a capability is taken in the project's Product tab.
no_work_body: Nothing syncs this deployment's issues and pull requests.
work_no_identifiers: The documents define no identifiers with a label (**ID**: `…`), so there is nothing for work to name.
work_names_none: No issue, pull request or commit names one of the {n} identifiers the documents define.
work_summary: {identifiers} identifiers defined in the documents; {total} named by work. {unlinked} of {work} issues, pull requests and commits name none. A piece of work is linked when its title, text or commit message names the identifier.
comparing: Comparing with the organization's other projects…
no_other_project: There is no other project in this organization you can read, so there is nothing to compare with.
nothing_similar_one: No requirement of the {count} other project reads like one of this project's.
nothing_similar_many: No requirement of the {count} other projects reads like one of this project's.
compared_one: Compared with {count} other project, by the words two statements share. Read both before deciding anything: a pair here is a question, not a finding.
compared_many: Compared with {count} other projects, by the words two statements share. Read both before deciding anything: a pair here is a question, not a finding.
compared_first_one: Compared with {count} other project (the first 40), by the words two statements share. Read both before deciding anything: a pair here is a question, not a finding.
compared_first_many: Compared with {count} other projects (the first 40), by the words two statements share. Read both before deciding anything: a pair here is a question, not a finding.
decision_reuse_why: The other project's functionality serves this need: use it rather than build it again
decision_coordinate_why: Related work: keep the two projects in step
decision_separate_why: Alike in words, different in what it does or for whom
decision_unrelated_why: Not the same functionality at all
coverage_hint: {extracted} read at their current revision, {failed} read part-way, {stale} changed since they were read, {pending} never read. A build reads only what is not read at its revision, so an unchanged document is never paid for twice. To read one document again, whatever its state, rebuild from it: only its facts are replaced.
kept_title: The repository copy is missing on the server: the last reading is shown
uploads_hint: CSV, JSON and plain-text files read into the model without committing them to the repository. Each is read under upload:<name> on the next build, like a document of the repository; its revision is the hash of its content. Uploading the same name again replaces it.
upload_pick: Upload a CSV, JSON or text file
upload_wrong_type: {name} is not CSV (.csv, .tsv), JSON (.json) or plain text (.txt)
no_uploads_body: Upload an export, a survey or an interview transcript for the model to read beside the repository.
